perspective:
From Carolyn Abebe’s available perspective:

- Carolyn knows she and Marilyn are colleagues at a community bank and have recently started working together.
- During a busy, stressful week at the bank, Carolyn noticed Marilyn had been unusually quiet and withdrawn for several days, which seemed unlike Marilyn’s normally engaged manner. Carolyn asked if everything was alright and whether Marilyn wanted to talk. Marilyn said she was overwhelmed by work and some personal stuff, and thanked Carolyn for asking.
- In a later interaction, Marilyn responded curtly. Carolyn felt confused and slightly hurt. Carolyn told Marilyn she hoped she hadn’t overstepped, said she had had tough times too, and that talking sometimes helps. Marilyn said she appreciated it, apologized if she seemed off, and said it had been a hard week.
- Carolyn perceived Marilyn’s response as positive and felt relieved and hopeful about their friendship. Carolyn invited Marilyn to a small weekend get-together with a few friends. Marilyn said it sounded lovely, thanked her, and said she would love to join.
- Although they had friendly interactions outside work, Carolyn felt Marilyn was still maintaining a professional distance at the bank. Carolyn felt disappointed and directly asked to talk about their work dynamic, saying she felt an unexplained distance between them. Marilyn said she hadn’t realized that, apologized if it seemed that way, and agreed to talk about improving collaboration.
- After their private talk/meeting, Carolyn believed they had cleared the air and better understood each other’s professional expectations and personal boundaries. She felt content and optimistic. Carolyn proposed teaming up on the new project proposal. Marilyn said that was a great idea, was glad they had talked, and looked forward to working more closely with her.
